expected_approaches.summary: Keep a min-heap containing the k largest values seen so far.
expected_approaches.applicability: When k is smaller than n and predictable bounded selection is desirable.
key_invariants: After each prefix, the heap contains its k largest values when at least k values have been seen.
The heap root is the kth largest value of that prefix.
tradeoffs: Predictable but more logarithmic work than expected-linear quickselect.
common_failure_modes: using a max heap of all values

expected_approaches.summary: Partition around pivots until the target sorted index is placed.
expected_approaches.applicability: In-memory selection when modifying an array copy is acceptable.
assumptions: Expected performance depends on pivot behavior.
key_invariants: After partitioning, values lie on the appropriate side of the pivot according to the chosen ordering.
expected_approaches.time_complexity: O(n) expected time; O(n^2) worst case
expected_approaches.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary for iterative in-place partitioning
tradeoffs: Faster expected selection but less predictable worst-case behavior.
common_implementation_variants: target index n-k in ascending order

alternative_approaches.summary: Sort the values and index the kth position in descending order.
alternative_approaches.applicability: A simple approach when O(n log n) is acceptable.
key_invariants: Sorted order places the requested ranked occurrence at a known index.
tradeoffs: Simplest but orders more data than selection requires.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: int findKthLargest(vector<int> nums,int k){ priority_queue<int,vector<int>,greater<int>> heap; for(int value:nums){heap.push(value);if((int)heap.size()>k)heap.pop();}return heap.top();} };

class Solution { public int findKthLargest(int[] nums,int k){ java.util.PriorityQueue<Integer> heap=new java.util.PriorityQueue<>(); for(int value:nums){heap.offer(value);if(heap.size()>k)heap.poll();}return heap.peek();} }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: The root is the smallest member of the retained k largest values.
Partition places values on the correct side of the pivot for target-index selection.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Derive O(n log k) rather than sorting all values.
Distinguish expected quickselect time from its quadratic worst case.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Do not claim expected pivot performance is a worst-case guarantee.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: A size-k heap must eject its smallest retained value.
Convert kth largest to the correct ascending index.

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: k equals one asks for the maximum.
k equals length asks for the minimum.

counterexamples.purpose: The second largest is still 5, not 4.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: A size-k heap naturally supports values arriving incrementally while full sorting and in-place quickselect do not.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend why the root is the kth largest retained rank.
Test expected versus worst-case quickselect complexity.

common_followups.diagnostic_goal: Test why the heap is a min-heap of size k.
weak_or_misconception_signals: keeps a max heap and ejects its largest
sample_phrasings: Why does removing the heap root preserve the kth-largest answer?
Where do equal values appear in the ranking?
What pivot behavior does your quickselect complexity rely on?

level_considerations.guidance: Focus on the size-k heap invariant and duplicate ranks.

reference_reasoning: The bounded min-heap is the primary reviewed prior; quickselect, sorting, and other plausible correct selection strategies remain independently evaluable.
